description: Bulk purchase 200 smartphones at $15 each, account created 2 days ago, VPN/proxy detected, shipping to freight forwarder
reason: Stolen card resale ring. Chargeback confirmed within 48h. Freight forwarder linked to 12 previous fraud cases.

description: Purchase 50 gift cards at $200 each from new account, email domain is disposable (guerrillamail)
reason: Gift card laundering. Cards redeemed within 1 hour across multiple accounts. Linked to organized ring.

description: Annual subscription upgrade from monthly, existing customer 3 years, same device fingerprint, no proxy
reason: Legitimate upgrade. Customer has consistent payment history, same billing address for 3 years.

description: Rapid-fire trial signups from same IP range, 15 accounts in 1 hour, all with similar email pattern (random+number@gmail)
reason: Trial abuse / account farming. Same device fingerprint across all signups. Goal: resell premium access.

description: Corporate bulk license purchase, 500 seats, wire transfer, verified business domain, existing B2B relationship
reason: Legitimate B2B purchase. Company verified via Dun & Bradstreet. High amount deviation is normal for enterprise deals.

description: Subscription with stolen card, address mismatch (billing: NYC, shipping: Lagos), high-value electronics bundle
reason: Classic card-not-present fraud. Address mismatch + proxy + high-value items. Chargeback filed by real cardholder.

description: Monthly renewal, autopay, customer since 2021, same payment method, watching patterns consistent
reason: Routine autopay renewal. Zero risk indicators. Consistent behavioral pattern over 4 years.

description: Account takeover: password changed, email changed, then immediate high-value purchase within 5 minutes
reason: Account takeover (ATO). Credential stuffing attack. Original owner reported unauthorized access 6 hours later.

description: Family plan upgrade, adding 3 members, existing customer, payment with card on file, residential IP
reason: Legitimate family plan expansion. Consistent with customer lifecycle (kids reaching streaming age).

description: Bulk discount code redemption, 30 codes applied across 30 accounts in 10 minutes, all from same subnet
reason: Promo code abuse. Codes leaked on forum, mass-redeemed by bot network. Revenue loss: $1,500.

description: Student discount purchase with valid .edu email, single subscription, low-cost plan, mobile device
reason: Legitimate student subscription. Email verified via university SSO integration.

description: Subscription purchased with prepaid virtual card, Tor exit node detected, new account, premium tier immediately
reason: Anonymized fraud attempt. Prepaid card + Tor = untraceable. Pattern matches carding forum tutorials.

description: Long-time customer switching from annual to monthly during known financial hardship period (post-holiday)
reason: Legitimate downgrade. Common pattern in January. Customer retained, lower tier but no churn.

description: Multiple failed payment attempts (5x), then success with different card, followed by immediate content download binge
reason: Card testing + successful fraud. First 5 cards were invalid (testing stolen batch). 6th worked. Downloaded all premium content within 30 min.

description: Business subscription renewal with updated card (old expired), same company domain, same admin user
reason: Normal card rotation due to expiration. All other signals unchanged. Zero risk.

description: Flash sale: 20 annual subscriptions purchased in 3 minutes, all shipped to same address, different cards
reason: Subscription stacking fraud during flash sale. Multiple stolen cards used to buy discounted annual plans for resale.

description: Senior citizen account, monthly auto-renewal, single device, consistent low-bandwidth usage, 5-year customer
reason: Completely routine. Elderly customer with predictable usage pattern. Model of low-risk subscriber.

description: Refund request immediately after purchase, then re-purchase with different promo code, repeated 4 times
reason: Refund abuse / promo exploitation. Customer exploiting refund-then-rebuy loophole to stack discounts.

description: International purchase from tourist IP (hotel WiFi in Japan), existing US customer, same device UUID
reason: Legitimate travel. IP geolocation mismatch explained by hotel WiFi. Device fingerprint confirms identity.

description: Credential sharing: single account streaming simultaneously from 8 different IPs across 3 countries
reason: Account sharing / credential selling. Single subscription resold on black market for shared access.

description: Black Friday purchase, existing customer, annual plan at 50% off, single transaction, home IP
reason: Legitimate Black Friday deal. Customer waited for sale (browsed pricing page 3x in prior week).

description: Synthetic identity: real SSN + fake name + new address, premium subscription, high-value add-ons
reason: Synthetic identity fraud. SSN belongs to minor/deceased. Identity built over months for this purchase.

description: Employee discount purchase, verified corporate email, single standard plan, payroll deduction
reason: Internal employee benefit. Verified via HR system integration. Payroll deduction = zero chargeback risk.

description: Charityware: 100 gift subscriptions purchased for shelter, corporate card, verified nonprofit, press release planned
reason: Legitimate charity bulk purchase. High volume + high amount but verified nonprofit with history.

description: Late-night purchase 3 AM, new card added, premium tier, VPN active, account dormant for 6 months
reason: Account compromise during dormancy. Attacker gained access via leaked credentials from other breach.

description: Returning customer resubscribing after 3-month break, same email, same card, win-back offer applied
reason: Win-back conversion. Customer left, received re-engagement email, returned. Normal lifecycle.

description: API-driven bulk subscription creation via partner integration, 200 accounts, OAuth token, rate-limited correctly
reason: Legitimate partner API integration. High velocity is expected (batch provisioning). OAuth verified.

description: Micro-transactions: 50 purchases of $0.99 add-ons in rapid succession, testing if card works before big purchase
reason: Card testing via micro-transactions. Fraudster validates stolen cards before making large purchase elsewhere.

description: Free tier user converting to paid after 30-day trial, consistent daily usage throughout trial, organic behavior
reason: Ideal trial-to-paid conversion. User engaged throughout trial. Healthy customer acquisition.

description: Coordinated attack: 15 different accounts, same device fingerprint, purchasing same premium plan within 2-minute window
reason: Coordinated bot attack. Single operator using browser automation. Device fingerprint hash identical across all accounts.
